audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Gideon call, altar destruction, and fleece-sign narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Midianite oppression, prophet rebuke, angel of YHWH, Gideon's fear and protest, altar meal sign, Baal altar destruction by night, Joash's defense, Jerubbaal naming, Spirit-clothing, tribal summons, and fleece signs.

verses.restored: Children of Israel did evil in eyes of YHWH, and YHWH gave them into hand of Midian seven years.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD: and the LORD delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years.

modern.text: Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD; so He delivered them into the hand of Midian for seven years,

original.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֧וּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֧ם יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד מִדְיָ֖ן שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים

verses.restored: Hand of Midian was strong over Israel; because of Midian, children of Israel made for themselves dens in mountains, caves, and strongholds.

familiar.text: And the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel: and because of the Midianites the children of Israel made them the dens which are in the mountains, and caves, and strong holds.

modern.text: and the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel. Because of the Midianites, the Israelites prepared shelters for themselves in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.

original.text: וַתָּ֥עָז יַד מִדְיָ֖ן עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִפְּנֵ֨י מִדְיָ֜ן עָשֽׂוּ לָהֶ֣ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶת הַמִּנְהָרוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וְאֶת הַמְּעָר֖וֹת וְאֶת הַמְּצָדֽוֹת

verses.restored: It was, when Israel sowed, that Midian, Amalek, and sons of east came up against them.

familiar.text: And so it was, when Israel had sown, that the Midianites came up, and the Amalekites, and the children of the east, even they came up against them;

modern.text: Whenever the Israelites would plant their crops, the Midianites, Amalekites, and other people of the east would come up and invade them,

original.text: וְהָיָ֖ה אִם זָרַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעָלָ֨ה מִדְיָ֧ן וַֽעֲמָלֵ֛ק וּבְנֵי קֶ֖דֶם וְעָל֥וּ עָלָֽיו

verses.restored: They camped against them and destroyed produce of land as far as Gaza; they left no sustenance in Israel, neither sheep nor ox nor donkey.

familiar.text: And they encamped against them, and destroyed the increase of the earth, till thou come unto Gaza, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass.

modern.text: encamping against them as far as Gaza and destroying the produce of the land. They left Israel with no sustenance, neither sheep nor oxen nor donkeys.

original.text: וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וַיַּשְׁחִ֨יתוּ֙ אֶת יְב֣וּל הָאָ֔רֶץ עַד בּוֹאֲךָ֖ עַזָּ֑ה וְלֹֽא יַשְׁאִ֤ירוּ מִֽחְיָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְשֶׂ֥ה וָשׁ֖וֹר וַחֲמֽוֹר

verses.restored: For they and their livestock came up, and their tents; they came like locusts for multitude, and they and their camels were without number; they came into land to ruin it.

familiar.text: For they came up with their cattle and their tents, and they came as grasshoppers for multitude; for both they and their camels were without number: and they entered into the land to destroy it.

modern.text: For the Midianites came with their livestock and their tents like a great swarm of locusts. They and their camels were innumerable, and they entered the land to ravage it.

original.text: כִּ֡י הֵם֩ וּמִקְנֵיהֶ֨ם יַעֲל֜וּ וְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם יבאו כְדֵֽי אַרְבֶּה֙ לָרֹ֔ב וְלָהֶ֥ם וְלִגְמַלֵּיהֶ֖ם אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ בָאָ֖רֶץ לְשַׁחֲתָֽהּ

verses.restored: Israel became very low because of Midian, and children of Israel cried out to YHWH.

familiar.text: And Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites; and the children of Israel cried unto the LORD.

modern.text: Israel was greatly impoverished by Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.

original.text: וַיִּדַּ֧ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מְאֹ֖ד מִפְּנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֑ן וַיִּזְעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: It was, when children of Israel cried out to YHWH because of Midian,

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD because of the Midianites,

modern.text: Now when the Israelites cried out to the LORD because of Midian,

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י כִּֽי זָעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל יְהוָ֑ה עַ֖ל אֹד֥וֹת מִדְיָֽן

verses.restored: that YHWH sent a man, a prophet, to children of Israel. He said to them, Thus says YHWH Divine of Israel: I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out from house of slaves.

familiar.text: That the LORD sent a prophet unto the children of Israel, which said unto them, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I brought you up from Egypt, and brought you forth out of the house of bondage;

modern.text: He sent them a prophet, who told them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought you up out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה אִ֥ישׁ נָבִ֖יא אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם כֹּה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָנֹכִ֞י הֶעֱלֵ֤יתִי אֶתְכֶם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וָאֹצִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים

verses.restored: I rescued you from hand of Egypt and from hand of all oppressing you; I drove them out before you and gave you their land.

familiar.text: And I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all that oppressed you, and drave them out from before you, and gave you their land;

modern.text: I delivered you out of the hands of Egypt and all your oppressors. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.

original.text: וָאַצִּ֤ל אֶתְכֶם֙ מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמִיַּ֖ד כָּל לֹחֲצֵיכֶ֑ם וָאֲגָרֵ֤שׁ אוֹתָם֙ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֔ם וָאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם אֶת אַרְצָֽם

verses.restored: I said to you, I am YHWH your Divine; you shall not fear gods of Amorite in whose land you dwell. But you did not listen to my voice.

familiar.text: And I said unto you, I am the LORD your God; fear not the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but ye have not obeyed my voice.

modern.text: And I said to you: ‘I am the LORD your God. You must not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.’ But you did not obey Me.” The Call of Gideon

original.text: וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָכֶ֗ם אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם לֹ֤א תִֽירְאוּ֙ אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים בְּאַרְצָ֑ם וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם בְּקוֹלִֽי

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH came and sat under terebinth at Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, while Gideon his son was beating wheat in winepress to hide it from Midian.

familiar.text: And there came an angel of the LORD, and sat under an oak which was in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abiezrite: and his son Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites.

modern.text: Then the angel of the LORD came and sat down under the oak in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, where his son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ תַּ֤חַת הָֽאֵלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָפְרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְיוֹאָ֖שׁ אֲבִ֣י הָֽעֶזְרִ֑י וְגִדְע֣וֹן בְּנ֗וֹ חֹבֵ֤ט חִטִּים֙ בַּגַּ֔ת לְהָנִ֖יס מִפְּנֵ֥י מִדְיָֽן

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH appeared to him and said to him, YHWH is with you, mighty man of strength.

familiar.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him, and said unto him, The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.

modern.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon and said, “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.”

original.text: וַיֵּרָ֥א אֵלָ֖יו מַלְּאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו יְהוָ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ גִּבּ֥וֹר הֶחָֽיִל

verses.restored: Gideon said to him, Please, my lord, if YHWH is with us, why then has all this found us? Where are all his wonders that our fathers recounted to us, saying, Did not YHWH bring us up from Egypt? But now YHWH has abandoned us and given us into palm of Midian.

familiar.text: And Gideon said unto him, Oh my Lord, if the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of, saying, Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt? but now the LORD hath forsaken us, and delivered us into the hands of the Midianites.

modern.text: “Please, my Lord,” Gideon replied, “if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? And where are all His wonders of which our fathers told us, saying, ‘Has not the LORD brought us up out of Egypt?’ But now the LORD has forsaken us and delivered us into the hand of Midian.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֤יו גִּדְעוֹן֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י וְיֵ֤שׁ יְהוָה֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ וְלָ֥מָּה מְצָאַ֖תְנוּ כָּל זֹ֑את וְאַיֵּ֣ה כָֽל נִפְלְאֹתָ֡יו אֲשֶׁר֩ סִפְּרוּ לָ֨נוּ אֲבוֹתֵ֜ינוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲלֹ֤א מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ הֶעֱלָ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה וְעַתָּה֙ נְטָשָׁ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖נוּ בְּכַף מִדְיָֽן

verses.restored: YHWH turned to him and said, Go in this strength of yours and save Israel from palm of Midian. Have I not sent you?

familiar.text: And the LORD looked upon him, and said, Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?

modern.text: The LORD turned to him and said, “Go in the strength you have and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not sending you?”

original.text: וַיִּ֤פֶן אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֵ֚ךְ בְּכֹחֲךָ֣ זֶ֔ה וְהוֹשַׁעְתָּ֥ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִכַּ֣ף מִדְיָ֑ן הֲלֹ֖א שְׁלַחְתִּֽיךָ

verses.restored: He said to him, Please, my lord, by what shall I save Israel? Look, my clan is weakest in Manasseh, and I am least in house of my father.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.

modern.text: “Please, my Lord,” Gideon replied, “how can I save Israel? Indeed, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s house.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָ֔י בַּמָּ֥ה אוֹשִׁ֖יעַ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנֵּ֤ה אַלְפִּי֙ הַדַּ֣ל בִּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה וְאָנֹכִ֥י הַצָּעִ֖יר בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽי

verses.restored: YHWH said to him, Surely I will be with you, and you shall strike Midian as one man.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto him, Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man.

modern.text: “Surely I will be with you,” the LORD replied, “and you will strike down all the Midianites as one man.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֶהְיֶ֖ה עִמָּ֑ךְ וְהִכִּיתָ֥ אֶת מִדְיָ֖ן כְּאִ֥ישׁ אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: He said to him, Please, if I have found favor in your eyes, make for me a sign that it is you speaking with me.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, If now I have found grace in thy sight, then shew me a sign that thou talkest with me.

modern.text: Gideon answered, “If I have found favor in Your sight, give me a sign that it is You speaking with me.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אִם נָ֛א מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ לִּי֙ א֔וֹת שָׁאַתָּ֖ה מְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמִּֽי

verses.restored: Please do not depart from here until I come to you, bring out my offering, and set it before you. He said, I will sit until you return.

familiar.text: Depart not hence, I pray thee, until I come unto thee, and bring forth my present, and set it before thee. And he said, I will tarry until thou come again.

modern.text: Please do not depart from this place until I return to You. Let me bring my offering and set it before You.” And the LORD said, “I will stay until you return.”

original.text: אַל נָ֨א תָמֻ֤שׁ מִזֶּה֙ עַד בֹּאִ֣י אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְהֹֽצֵאתִי֙ אֶת מִנְחָתִ֔י וְהִנַּחְתִּ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אָנֹכִ֥י אֵשֵׁ֖ב עַ֥ד שׁוּבֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Gideon went and prepared a kid of goats and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour; meat he put in basket and broth he put in pot, brought them out to him under terebinth, and presented them.

familiar.text: And Gideon went in, and made ready a kid, and unleavened cakes of an ephah of flour: the flesh he put in a basket, and he put the broth in a pot, and brought it out unto him under the oak, and presented it.

modern.text: So Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened bread and an ephah of flour. He placed the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot and brought them out to present to Him under the oak.

original.text: וְגִדְע֣וֹן בָּ֗א וַיַּ֤עַשׂ גְּדִֽי עִזִּים֙ וְאֵיפַת קֶ֣מַח מַצּ֔וֹת הַבָּשָׂר֙ שָׂ֣ם בַּסַּ֔ל וְהַמָּרַ֖ק שָׂ֣ם בַּפָּר֑וּר וַיּוֹצֵ֥א אֵלָ֛יו אֶל תַּ֥חַת הָאֵלָ֖ה וַיַּגַּֽשׁ

verses.restored: Messenger of Divine said to him, Take meat and unleavened cakes and place them on this rock, and pour out broth. He did so.

familiar.text: And the angel of God said unto him, Take the flesh and the unleavened cakes, and lay them upon this rock, and pour out the broth. And he did so.

modern.text: And the angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened bread, lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” And Gideon did so.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים קַ֣ח אֶת הַבָּשָׂ֤ר וְאֶת הַמַּצּוֹת֙ וְהַנַּח֙ אֶל הַסֶּ֣לַע הַלָּ֔ז וְאֶת הַמָּרַ֖ק שְׁפ֑וֹךְ וַיַּ֖עַשׂ כֵּֽן

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH stretched out end of staff in his hand and touched meat and unleavened cakes; fire rose from rock and consumed meat and unleavened cakes, and messenger of YHWH went from his eyes.

familiar.text: Then the angel of the LORD put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there rose up fire out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes. Then the angel of the LORD departed out of his sight.

modern.text: Then the angel of the LORD extended the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread. And fire flared from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread. Then the angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה אֶת קְצֵ֤ה הַמִּשְׁעֶ֨נֶת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָד֔וֹ וַיִּגַּ֥ע בַּבָּשָׂ֖ר וּבַמַּצּ֑וֹת וַתַּ֨עַל הָאֵ֜שׁ מִן הַצּ֗וּר וַתֹּ֤אכַל אֶת הַבָּשָׂר֙ וְאֶת הַמַּצּ֔וֹת וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה הָלַ֖ךְ מֵעֵינָֽיו

verses.restored: Gideon saw that he was messenger of YHWH, and Gideon said, Alas, Lord YHWH! For I have seen messenger of YHWH face to face.

familiar.text: And when Gideon perceived that he was an angel of the LORD, Gideon said, Alas, O LORD God! for because I have seen an angel of the LORD face to face.

modern.text: When Gideon realized that it was the angel of the LORD, he said, “Oh no, Lord GOD! I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!”

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא גִּדְע֔וֹן כִּֽי מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה ה֑וּא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גִּדְע֗וֹן אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כִּֽי עַל כֵּ֤ן רָאִ֨יתִי֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה פָּנִ֖ים אֶל פָּנִֽים

verses.restored: YHWH said to him, Peace to you; do not fear; you shall not die.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto him, Peace be unto thee; fear not: thou shalt not die.

modern.text: But the LORD said to him, “Peace be with you. Do not be afraid, for you will not die.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֧וֹ יְהוָ֛ה שָׁל֥וֹם לְךָ֖ אַל תִּירָ֑א לֹ֖א תָּמֽוּת

verses.restored: Gideon built there an altar to YHWH and called it YHWH-shalom/YHWH is peace; to this day it is still in Ophrah of Abiezrites.

familiar.text: Then Gideon built an altar there unto the LORD, and called it Jehovahshalom: unto this day it is yet in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

modern.text: So Gideon built an altar to the LORD there and called it The LORD Is Peace. To this day it stands in Ophrah of the Abiezrites. Gideon Destroys Baal’s Altar

translation_notes: Midianite oppression is described as economic devastation: crops, animals, security, and ordinary dwelling collapse until Israel hides in caves and cries out.
Gideon's first speech resists easy triumphalism: he asks why suffering has found the people if YHWH is with them.
YHWH names Gideon 'mighty man of strength' while Gideon is hiding wheat, making courage compatible with fear and survival behavior.
Gideon's altar is called YHWH-shalom after he survives the Divine encounter; peace appears before the war narrative resumes.

The Baal/Asherah destruction is internal covenant confrontation in ancient Israelite narrative. It must not authorize modern religious vandalism, persecution, or violence against polytheists, pagans, or other faith communities.
Joash's defense—if Baal is a god, let him contend for himself—de-escalates a mob death demand, though it still contains retaliatory threat language.
The Spirit 'clothed' Gideon, a vivid embodiment image rather than possession language to exploit for coercive leadership claims.
The fleece signs show Gideon's fear and need for confirmation; they should not become a manipulative testing formula or proof that every anxious person must demand signs.
safety_note: Do not use Judges 6 to justify religious vandalism, persecution, mob punishment, coercive sign-seeking, or shaming fearful people. Center economic oppression, honest protest, courage inside fear, de-escalation of mob violence, and Divine peace before militarized action.
